name: Hermitage

limits: For red wine, Syrah: at least 85%

climate.koppen_name: Temperate, no dry season, hot summer

terms: France's protected place names. A wine sold under one must follow that appellation's rules. The EU's term for the same tier is PDO, or AOP in French.
keyfacts: Appellation rules allow Syrah to be topped up with 15% or less of Marsanne and/or Roussanne.
Vin de paille, or straw wine, is also produced in the region.

notes: Hermitage reds tend to be very earthy, with aromas of leather, red berries, earth, cocoa and coffee.
They are mineral and tannic, with a long reputation for power.
Rich, dry whites are made from Marsanne and Roussanne.

blurb.text: A northern Rhône appellation on a hill south of Lyon, making mostly red wine from Syrah. The white, from Marsanne and Roussanne, is around 30% of the wine. Some see the hill as the spiritual home of Syrah.
